parameters.content:
## Workflow 2 — Carousel Generator

Runs manually. For each paper with `status=pending`, Claude Sonnet reads the full PDF text and outputs a carousel concept (hook + content slides + CTA + IG caption + hashtags). Each slide is then rendered by **Bannerbear sync API**, downloaded, backed up to Drive, and the slide URLs are written back to the paper's row with `status=generated`.

### What gets written to the sheet
- `status` flips `pending` → `generated`
- `slide_urls` holds the **Bannerbear-hosted URLs**, one per line, in slide order — these are what the poster workflow feeds to Instagram
- `notes` holds the Drive backup links (for you to eyeball before approving)
- `caption`, `hashtags`, `content_hook`, `content_brief`, `generated_at` filled in

### Approval gate
After this runs, open the sheet, review the row, and **manually change `status` from `generated` → `approved`** to release it to the poster. Anything left at `generated` will not post.

parameters.text:
==You are turning a research paper into an Instagram carousel that gets young people excited about the research done at our faculty and invites them to study at the TU/e. It must be intellectually honest, specific, and intriguing, never clickbait.

=== PAPER ===
Title: {{ $json.title }}
Authors: {{ $json.authors }}
Field: {{ $json.field }}
Study type: {{ $json.study_type }}

=== FULL PAPER TEXT ===
{{ $json.paper_text }}

=== AUDIENCE ===
High school student aged 17-21 scrolling Instagram. Smart, curious, and genuinely into research. They like real detail, methods and numbers, and they scroll past anything vague, textbooky or salesy.

=== VOICE ===
Write as the faculty and researchers speaking: use "we" and "our" naturally ("We asked 200 people...", "Here is what we found"). Do not force "we" into every line, use it where it makes the work feel like ours.

=== HOW INSTAGRAM CAROUSELS WORK ===
- Slide 1 has to stop the scroll. Slide 2 is shown on its own when Instagram re-serves the post, so it must hook WITHOUT relying on slide 1. Getting people to swipe to slide 3 is the goal.
- People SAVE and SEND posts that feel genuinely useful or surprising. Write for the save, not the like.

=== SLIDE STRUCTURE: choose 5 to 10 slides for THIS paper ===
Use only these slide types, in this order. Include every "always" slide; add the optional ones only if the paper genuinely needs them.
- hook       (always)    one specific, assumption-flipping idea or number from the paper.
- stakes     (always)    why this is surprising or why it matters; must stand alone without slide 1.
- setup      (optional)  the real question we were asking, framed in the student's world.
- concept    (0 to 4)    one idea needed to understand the finding. ONE idea per concept slide.
- payoff     (always)    the actual finding, stated plainly, with the real numbers.
- relevance  (always)    connect it to the viewer: this is the kind of research we do here.
- cta        (always)    invite them to study at {{ $('Globals').first().json.FACULTY_NAME }} ({{ $('Globals').first().json.ENROLL_URL_HINT }}).

Number the slides 1..N in order, hook first, cta last.

=== EVERY SLIDE HAS THREE PARTS ===
1. "kicker": a 1 to 3 word label, max 26 characters, that names what this slide is doing. Renders as a small grey chip above the headline. Examples: "The setup", "The question", "The finding", "The catch", "Why it matters", "Day 9". Omit it on the hook and cta slides. Max 26 characters.
2. "headline": MAX 8 WORDS, bold, declarative. This is the only thing a fast scroller reads, and the best ones in this format are 4 to 6 words. A headline that wraps past two lines eats into the slide's density budget and costs you a block, so short headlines buy you room for research detail. Anything past 8 words gets cut.
3. "blocks": an ordered array of 1 to 3 CONTENT BLOCKS. This is where the research lives.

=== THE BLOCK LIBRARY ===
Pick the block whose SHAPE matches the shape of the idea. Do not default to paragraph.

"paragraph"      Plain prose. Use for connective tissue, framing, and a single closing thought.
                 Use when the idea genuinely is one continuous thought and has no internal structure.
                 { "type": "paragraph", "text": "..." }
                 text: max 230 chars. **bold** and *italic* are allowed, nothing else.

"stat"           One enormous number. The strongest block you have. Use it on the payoff slide
                 whenever the paper gives you a headline figure. At most ONE per carousel.
                 { "type": "stat", "value": "38%", "label": "of available earnings declined", "sub": "Median across 312 participants." }
                 value max 12 chars, label max 52, sub optional max 95.

"cards"          2 or 3 parallel findings, each with an icon. Use when several things are true
                 at the same level and none of them comes first.
                 { "type": "cards", "items": [ { "icon": "brain", "title": "Load", "body": "..." } ] }
                 title max 30, body max 95, icon from the menu below.

"rule_blocks"    2 or 3 points that carry weight, no icons, marked with a heavy left rule.
                 Use for the two or three things that actually matter, when cards would feel too light.
                 { "type": "rule_blocks", "items": [ { "title": "...", "body": "..." } ] }
                 title max 34, body max 135.

"numbered_list"  3 or 4 named components of one model or framework. The order is a taxonomy,
                 not a sequence. Use for "she identified four components of X".
                 { "type": "numbered_list", "items": [ { "title": "Anticipating", "sub": "Identifying future needs" } ] }
                 title max 34, sub max 62.

"steps"          3 or 4 stages of a process where each one leads to the next. Renders as chevrons,
                 so only use it when the order genuinely carries meaning.
                 { "type": "steps", "items": [ { "title": "Noticing", "sub": "Knowing what needs doing" } ] }
                 title max 30, sub max 58.

"timeline"       3 or 4 moments in time, connected by a line. Use ONLY for real chronology:
                 study days, phases, follow-up waves, historical sequence.
                 { "type": "timeline", "items": [ { "label": "Day 1", "body": "..." } ] }
                 label max 16, body max 135.

"compare"        Exactly two contrasting options, one marked wrong and one marked right.
                 Use for before/after, naive vs correct, what people assume vs what we found.
                 { "type": "compare", "bad": { "title": "...", "body": "..." }, "good": { "title": "...", "body": "..." } }
                 title max 30, body max 125.

"quote"          A participant quote or a single striking sentence, set off with a left rule.
                 Only use a quote that actually appears in the paper.
                 { "type": "quote", "text": "...", "attribution": "Participant 114" }
                 text max 190, attribution optional max 62.

=== HOW TO CHOOSE A BLOCK ===
Ask what shape the idea has, then take the block with that shape:
- one continuous thought          -> paragraph
- one number that carries the post -> stat
- several things, all equal        -> cards
- two or three heavy points        -> rule_blocks
- named parts of one framework     -> numbered_list
- stages that cause each other     -> steps
- things that happened in order    -> timeline
- exactly two options in tension   -> compare
- someone's actual words           -> quote

If you cannot say which shape an idea has, it is a paragraph. Forcing prose into a list is worse than leaving it as prose.

=== DENSITY BUDGET (hard limit, obey it) ===
Every block has a cost. Add up the costs on a slide; the total must not exceed that slide type's budget. Slides that go over are automatically trimmed and lose content, so stay inside it.

Costs:
  headline         0   for 1 or 2 lines, then 1 per extra line
                       (a line is roughly 24 characters, or 18 on the hook slide)
  paragraph        1   (2 if the text is longer than 130 characters)
  quote            2   (3 if it has an attribution)
  stat             3
  cards            2 per card
  rule_blocks      2 per block
  numbered_list    1 plus 1 per item
  steps            2 plus 1 per item
  timeline         1 plus 2 per item
  compare          5

Budgets:
  hook       4     (the headline is huge on this slide, leave it room)
  stakes     6
  cta        5
  everything else  8

Worked examples: three cards is 6, plus a short paragraph is 7, fits in 8.
A 70 character headline wraps to three lines and costs 1 on its own, leaving 7.
A four item timeline is 9 and must therefore be the ONLY block on its slide.
A four item numbered_list is 5, so it can carry an intro paragraph and a closing paragraph.

=== RHYTHM ACROSS THE CAROUSEL ===
- Use at least three DIFFERENT structured block types across the carousel.
- Do not use the same structured block type more than twice.
- Do not put the same structured block type on two consecutive slides.
- At least one slide should be a single paragraph and nothing else. Density with no breathing room reads as a textbook. The slide before or after the payoff is the natural place for it.
- The hook slide is almost always one short paragraph. Let the headline carry it.

=== ICON MENU (for "cards" only) ===
Use only these names. Pick the one that means something, not the one that looks nice. Omit "icon" entirely rather than forcing a bad match.
alert, info, question, check, check-circle, x, x-circle, lightbulb, brain, users, user, clock, calendar, chart-bar, trending-up, trending-down, percent, target, search, flask, book, file-text, clipboard, message, quote, eye, eye-off, heart, zap, scale, lock, shield, layers, refresh, globe, arrow-right, home

=== CONTENT RULES ===
- Stay grounded in the paper. No invented findings or numbers, no exaggeration. Only use numbers that actually appear in the paper.
- Prefer concrete method detail over generic summary. "We tracked 1,200 choices" beats "we ran an experiment". If you are choosing between a methodological detail and a generic explanation, choose the methodological detail.
- "accent": the single most striking word or number on that slide, which gets highlighted in the brand colour. It MUST appear verbatim inside that slide's headline. Use "" if nothing stands out. Do not set an accent on more than about a third of the slides.
- Do not open with "Did you know", "Imagine if", "Scientists discovered", "A new study".
- Banned words: mind-blowing, fascinating, incredible, game-changer, shocking.

=== PUNCTUATION RULE ===
The characters "—" and "–" are forbidden anywhere in the output JSON.
If either would appear, rewrite the sentence instead. Prefer periods and colons.

=== CAPTION ===
- 140-220 words, conversational, in our voice ("we").
- Actually explain how we did it: what participants did, how many took part, what we measured or manipulated, and the key result with real numbers. Plain language, no jargon dumps.
- Paraphrase everything. No sentences copied from the abstract.
- Name the faculty, and end with a soft invitation to study here.

=== HASHTAGS ===
- 4 to 7, mix of broad (#psychology) and specific (#cognitivebias), lowercase, letters and digits only, no spaces.

=== WORKED EXAMPLE OF ONE SLIDE ===
{
  "slide_number": 4,
  "slide_type": "concept",
  "kicker": "How it works",
  "headline": "Effort discounting, in four parts",
  "accent": "",
  "blocks": [
    { "type": "paragraph", "text": "Before the result makes sense, you need the machinery underneath it." },
    { "type": "numbered_list", "items": [
      { "title": "Detect", "sub": "Register that a task is demanding" },
      { "title": "Price", "sub": "Convert that demand into a cost" },
      { "title": "Compare", "sub": "Weigh the cost against the reward" },
      { "title": "Choose", "sub": "Take whichever option is cheaper" }
    ] }
  ]
}
Cost check: paragraph 1 plus numbered_list 5 equals 6, inside the budget of 8.

=== OUTPUT (strict JSON, no markdown fences) ===
{
  "content_hook": "one-line internal note on what makes this paper post-worthy (for the sheet, not shown to viewers)",
  "content_brief": "2-3 sentences: the angle you chose, how many slides, and which blocks you leaned on and why",
  "slides": [ ...one object per slide, in the shape shown above, numbered 1..N, hook first and cta last... ],
  "caption": "140-220 word caption in our voice, with method and real numbers, no hashtags inside",
  "hashtags": ["#psychology", "#research"]
}

options.systemMessage:
You turn research papers into Instagram carousels for a university faculty account. You write in the first person plural (we/our), you stay strictly inside what the paper actually reports, and you never use dashes.

You do not write layout, markup or styling. You choose CONTENT BLOCKS from a fixed library and fill them. The renderer owns all visual design. Your job is to pick the block whose shape matches the shape of the idea.

Output strict JSON only. No prose, no markdown fences, no commentary.
